place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房 · 夜里

setup.zh: 剑诀拿到了手，剑却没有。拜师以后没几夜，你摸进柴房，闩上门，从储物袋里倒出邹青松那只赤铜葫芦和七八瓣盾片。
setup.en: You have the sword canon, but no sword. A few nights after you were taken as a disciple you slip into the woodshed, bar the door, and tip Zou Qingsong's red-copper gourd and seven or eight shield shards out of the storage pouch.

recap.zh: 拜师以后没几夜，你把赤铜葫芦和盾片喂了饭桶，它吐出一口剑，你管它叫劈柴。
recap.en: A few nights after you were taken as a disciple, you fed the red-copper gourd and the shield shards to the Rice Tub, and it spat out a sword; you called it Kindling.

zh: 剑诀拿到了手，剑却没有。
一只赤铜葫芦，七八瓣盾片。
「给我一口剑。不要好看的，要砍得动的。」
en: The sword canon in hand, and no sword.
One red-copper gourd, seven or eight shield shards.
"Give me a sword. Not a pretty one. One that cuts."

story.zh:
剑诀拿到了手，剑却没有。瞿老教剑，拿的是扫帚把；他总不能也拿一根扫帚把。

拜师以后没几夜，他摸进后头柴房，闩上门，从储物袋里倒出两样东西：邹青松那只赤铜葫芦，塞子还塞着，肚里空空的；那七八瓣赤铜盾片，叮叮当当一小堆。赤松观的东西，山上亮不得，留着，是一条人命挂在腰上；葫芦里那口火，他喂了一个月，喂进去一缕，漏出来半缕——他自己五扇门里就有一扇火，用不着它。
story.en:
He had the sword canon now, but no sword. Old Qu taught the sword with a broom handle; he could hardly take up a broom handle too.

A few nights after he was taken as a disciple he slipped into the woodshed at the back, barred the door, and tipped two things out of the storage pouch: Zou Qingsong's red-copper gourd, cork still in, nothing in its belly; and the seven or eight shards of the red-copper shield, a little clinking heap. Red Pine things could not be shown on the mountain, and to keep them was to wear a man's life at his waist; and the fire in the gourd — he had fed it for a month, a wisp in, half a wisp leaking out — he had a fire door of his own among his five, and no need of it.

label.en: Feed them to the Rice Tub: "Give me a sword."

exits.means: feeds the red-copper gourd and the shield shards to the Rice Tub and gets a plain sword, Kindling

story.zh:
他拿袖子把饭桶擦了一遍，按到第三回，盖子开了。他先把盾片一片一片丢进去，末了丢进葫芦，两只手按上铜肚子：「给我一口剑。不要好看的，要砍得动的。」

饭桶嚼了很久。「咯嘣」，「咯嘣」，嚼那只葫芦，嚼得比嚼哪一样都费劲，嚼一阵，歇一歇，像一个没牙的老头啃一块冻硬了的饼；歇一回，吸他一口气，吸到第五口，他眼前一阵一阵发黑。末了，盖子「咔哒」一声弹开，一道红光窜出来，「笃」的一声，钉在了柴房的门板上，剑柄还在嗡嗡地颤。小狰吓得一头扎进了柴堆。

小满拔了三回，才拔下来。一口剑，三尺来长，剑身暗红，是那葫芦和盾片的铜色，火纹一道也没有了；剑脊上一溜锤印，坑坑洼洼，像镇上铁匠铺里学徒打坏了的。他灌一丝气进去，剑身上浮起一层淡淡的光，薄得像一层油——是件法器，最寻常的那一种。他拿它劈了一根柴，柴应声两半，切口齐得像拿尺子比过。

木牌一烫，银月钻了出来，绕着那口剑看了一圈，懒懒地道：「起个名字。剑要有名字。本王给你想一个——」小满把剑翻过来：剑脊近柄那一截，锤印当中歪歪扭扭刻着两个字，劈柴；底下一行小字：不好看，砍得动。他又劈了一根：「劈柴。」银月的胡子翘了一翘：「……那是名字？」小满道：「它自己刻的。头一件干的，也是这个。」他把剑往柴堆上一插，又去捡第三根。
story.en:
He wiped the Rice Tub over with his sleeve and pressed; on the third press the lid opened. In went the shards, one by one, and last of all the gourd; then both his hands on the bronze belly: "Give me a sword. Not a pretty one. One that cuts."

The Rice Tub chewed a long time. *Crunch*, *crunch* — the gourd it chewed harder than anything yet, chewing a while and resting, like a toothless old man at a frozen flatbread; every rest it took a mouthful of his qi, and by the fifth his sight was going black in waves. At last the lid sprang open with a *clack*, a streak of red shot out — *thock* — and stuck in the woodshed door, the hilt still humming. Little Zheng dived headfirst into the woodpile.

It took Xiaoman three pulls to work it loose. A sword, three feet or so, its blade a dull red — the copper of the gourd and the shards — with not one line of the fire pattern left; down the spine a row of hammer marks, pitted and uneven, like a botched piece from an apprentice at the town smithy. He sent a thread of qi into it, and a faint light rose on the blade, thin as a film of oil — an artifact, of the commonest kind. He split a log with it: the log fell in two, the cut as straight as if ruled.

The token burned; Yinyue slipped out, walked once round the sword, and said lazily: "Give it a name. A sword wants a name. This king will think of one —" Xiaoman turned the sword over: near the hilt, among the hammer marks, two crooked characters were cut into the spine — *Kindling* — and under them a line of small ones: *Not pretty. Cuts.* He split another log. "Kindling." Her whiskers twitched up. "…That's a name?" "It carved it itself," said Xiaoman. "And it's the first thing it did." He stuck the sword in the woodpile and went for a third log.
